## What Google's AI Mode Means for a Digital Marketing Agency in Pune

Google's AI Mode is a separate, conversational search experience that runs multiple background searches to answer a query in depth, rather than the single synthesised summary you see in AI Overviews. For a digital marketing agency in Pune advising local and national clients, the practical difference is this: AI Mode changes not just what shows up on a results page, but how a search session works from start to finish, and that has real consequences for content strategy, ad spend, and what you can actually measure.

This article separates what is confirmed about AI Mode from what is still rolling out, walks through how it differs operationally from AI Overviews and classic organic and paid results, and lays out what we think agencies and business owners in Pune should be doing differently because of it.

### A quick note on sourcing

Everything below is based on Google's own product announcements and reporting from Search Engine Land and Search Engine Journal, linked at the end. Where the public record is thin or still changing — India-specific timing in particular — we say so directly instead of guessing.

## AI Mode vs AI Overviews: Not the Same Feature

These two are often talked about interchangeably, which causes confusion when clients ask "are we showing up in the AI thing yet?" They are not the same feature, and they behave differently enough that treating them as one is a mistake.

AI Overviews are the AI-generated summary boxes that can appear automatically at the top of a normal Google Search results page for certain queries. You don't have to do anything to see one — Google decides when a query qualifies, and the summary sits above the traditional blue links, which remain visible below it.

AI Mode is a distinct, dedicated tab and experience inside Search (and the Google app) that a user actively chooses. Instead of a single query and a single summary, AI Mode is built for a conversation: you ask something, get a synthesised answer, then ask a follow-up, and the system keeps context across that exchange the way a chat-based assistant does. According to Google's own product coverage, AI Mode uses custom Gemini models with what Google describes as advanced reasoning and multimodal understanding, and it accepts typed, voice, or image (via Lens) input.

### Query fan-out: the mechanism behind AI Mode

The technical piece that explains most of the practical differences is something Google and outside reporting refer to as "query fan-out." Rather than answering your question with one search, AI Mode breaks it into several related sub-questions, runs searches for each of those in the background, and then synthesises everything into one response. Search Engine Land's reporting on AI Mode's language expansion describes this directly: the system "simultaneously issues multiple related searches across subtopics and data sources, then synthesises results," which Google says gives users more breadth and depth than a traditional single search.

This matters for content strategy for one simple reason: a page that only answers the literal, narrow query a user typed is competing against a system that is actively looking for related sub-answers too. A page structured to also answer the two or three adjacent questions a reader would naturally ask next has more surface area to be pulled into that fan-out process.

## AI Mode vs AI Overviews vs Classic Organic Results

The table below is the version of this comparison we actually use internally when explaining the shift to clients. It focuses on what triggers each experience, how content needs to differ to be well-positioned for it, and — importantly — what you can currently measure for each in standard analytics tools.

| | Classic Organic Results | AI Overviews | AI Mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| **What triggers it** | Any standard search query | Automatically, for certain informational/comparison queries Google judges suitable for a summary | Only when a user actively opens the AI Mode tab/experience, or asks a follow-up within it |
| **User experience** | List of ranked links with titles, snippets, sometimes rich results | A generated summary block above the normal results, with the normal results still visible below | A standalone, chat-style thread — user asks, gets an answer, can keep asking follow-ups with context retained |
| **Underlying mechanism** | Classic crawling, indexing and ranking signals | A generative summary drawing on a smaller set of sources, shown alongside normal ranking | Query fan-out — multiple related background searches synthesised into one deeper answer, using Gemini models |
| **What content needs to do** | Match search intent, target keywords, earn links and authority signals | Be extractable and clearly structured so a snippet-style answer can be lifted from it | Also answer the adjacent, follow-up questions a real conversation would raise, not just the headline query |
| **Ads** | Standard Search ads above/around results | Ads can still appear on the page around the overview | Google has begun testing and rolling out dedicated ad formats built for the conversational format (see the ads section below) |
| **What's measurable today** | Full keyword-level data in Search Console and analytics | Impressions/clicks are counted but not broken out separately from regular Search in most standard reporting | According to Search Engine Land's reporting, AI Mode query data is logged in Search Console but currently lumped in with standard Search data, so isolating its specific performance is not straightforward yet |

The last row is the one clients push back on most, and it's worth being blunt about: as of now, there is no clean, separated "AI Mode performance" report sitting inside Google Search Console the way there is for, say, mobile versus desktop. That's a real reporting gap, not a vendor limitation, and any agency telling you otherwise is overstating what's currently available.

## Where AI Mode Actually Stands in India Right Now

This is the section where it's important to be precise rather than promotional, because rollout timelines get exaggerated constantly in marketing content.

Based on Google's own announcements: AI Mode was introduced in India as a Search Labs experiment in June 2025, then opened to all users without a Labs opt-in shortly after, in English only at that stage. Hindi support followed in September 2025, alongside four other languages (Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, and Brazilian Portuguese), as part of a broader push beyond English. Google has separately said it went on to add more Indian languages and brought its Search Live feature (real-time voice/camera search) to India in both English and Hindi, making India one of the first markets outside the US to get that combination.

By early-to-mid 2026, Google's public messaging describes AI Mode as available in well over 200 countries and territories and roughly 100 languages worldwide, following further expansion rounds. What is not fully clear from the public record is the exact, current depth of AI Mode's language and regional-dialect coverage inside India — for example, how consistently it performs across regional Indian languages beyond Hindi, or how usage compares between Hindi and English queries in Indian cities. We have not found reporting precise enough to state figures on that, so we are not going to invent them. If a claim like that shows up in someone else's blog post citing a specific percentage of Indian searches happening in AI Mode, treat it with real skepticism unless it links to a primary source.

What we can say with confidence is the direction of travel: Google has moved fast on language and geography for AI Mode compared to how slowly some past Search features rolled out internationally, and India was an early priority market, not an afterthought. That alone is reason enough for a business with an Indian audience to start adjusting content now rather than waiting for a fully mature reporting picture.

## How This Changes the Search Behaviour of Your Customers

Before getting into tactics, it's worth naming what actually changes for the person searching, because that's what tactics should respond to.

In classic search, a user types a query, scans a page of results, and clicks through to one or more sites to get their answer. In an AI Overview, a chunk of that scanning-and-clicking work gets replaced by reading a summary first — some users still click through, many don't. In AI Mode, the entire session can happen without leaving Google at all: a user researching, say, "best CRM for a small services business in Pune" can ask that, get a synthesised comparison, ask "which of these have good local support," ask "what would implementation cost roughly," and never visit a single vendor website until they've already narrowed their shortlist.

That's a meaningfully different funnel. The awareness and early-consideration stages of a purchase journey can now happen entirely inside a Google conversation. By the time a prospective customer does click through to a website, they may already be much closer to a decision — which changes what that landing page needs to do, and changes how top-of-funnel traffic numbers should be interpreted.

## What a Digital Marketing Agency in Pune Should Change: Content Strategy

This is the operational core of the article — the actual changes we think are justified by what's confirmed above, not speculation dressed up as certainty.

### Write for the follow-up question, not just the headline query

Because AI Mode fans a single query out into several related searches, a page that only answers the exact phrase a user might type is leaving coverage on the table. If you publish a page targeting "digital marketing agency in Pune," it should also naturally answer the two or three things someone asking that question would want to know next — what services are typically included, how pricing generally works in the market, how long results usually take, what questions to ask before signing on. Structuring a single comprehensive page around a main question plus its natural follow-ups gives you more chances to be a source for the fan-out searches AI Mode runs behind the scenes.

### Strengthen E-E-A-T signals deliberately

Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness and Trustworthiness were already part of Google's quality guidance long before AI Mode existed, but they matter more now because a generative system is deciding, on the fly, which sources are trustworthy enough to draw from and cite. Concretely, that means: visible author information and real credentials on advice content, clear "who runs this business" information, genuine client testimonials and reviews (never fabricated ones), and content that reads like it was written by someone who has actually done the work, not generic filler.

### Use structured data properly

Schema markup — Organization, LocalBusiness, FAQPage, Article, Review schema where genuinely applicable — helps both traditional Search and generative systems understand what a page is, who published it, and how its content is organised. It doesn't guarantee inclusion in an AI-generated answer, but it removes ambiguity that could otherwise cause a system to skip a page in favour of a competitor's more clearly-marked-up one.

### Lean on first-party data and specificity

Generic, templated marketing copy is the easiest thing for a generative summary to skip past, because it says nothing a dozen other pages don't also say. Original data points, genuinely specific local detail, and direct, unhedged answers to real questions are harder to route around. This is also why our [SEO service](/services/seo/) work leans heavily on original content rather than templated pages — it's a stronger position for exactly this kind of shift.

## What Changes in Reporting and Client Conversations

The measurement gap described in the comparison table above is going to be an ongoing conversation with clients for a while yet. Search Console currently reports AI Mode-driven impressions and clicks blended into regular Search totals rather than as a separate, filterable channel. That means:

- A visible rise in impressions with a flatter click-through rate could be a sign of AI Mode surfacing your content without users clicking through immediately — but you cannot currently isolate and confirm that from Search Console data alone.
- Brand-search and direct-traffic trends become a more important secondary signal, since a user who researched a decision inside an AI Mode conversation may arrive at a site later by typing the business name directly rather than clicking a see-all-results link.
- Agencies should be honest with clients that "AI Mode performance" is not yet a reportable line item the way keyword rankings are, and set expectations accordingly rather than presenting invented dashboards as more precise than they can be.

## Ads in AI Mode: What Changes for Paid Search

Ads are already appearing inside AI Mode, and the trend is toward more integration rather than less. Search Engine Land's July 2026 study of AI Mode ad behaviour found ads present in close to 30% of commercial queries analysed, with ad presence rising sharply for higher cost-per-click keyword categories — from roughly a quarter of low-CPC queries up to over half of the highest-CPC ones. The same study found that a large majority of advertisers showing ads in AI Mode did not also rank organically for those same terms, and that most advertising domains were not among the sources cited in the AI-generated answer itself — meaning paid visibility and organic/citation visibility inside AI Mode currently behave as fairly separate tracks.

Separately, Google has begun rolling out new, more conversational ad formats built specifically for AI-powered Search — described in its own announcements as things like Conversational Discovery ads and AI-powered Shopping ads, designed to answer a specific question directly inside the AI Mode thread rather than sitting beside it as a traditional banner. These formats are still new and evolving, and how well they perform for a typical Pune-based service business isn't established yet from independently verified case data — so we're describing this as a direction to watch and test cautiously, not a proven playbook. If you're already running Google Ads, this is worth a conversation with whoever manages your [Google Ads](/services/google-ads/) account about testing budget carefully rather than assuming legacy campaign structures translate directly.

## Our View at Govindani Infotech

We're not going to pretend this shift has settled into a fixed playbook yet — anyone claiming a fully proven AI Mode strategy this early is overselling it. Our approach for marketing clients is to treat AI Mode as a reason to double down on fundamentals that were already good practice — genuinely useful, specific, well-structured content, clean technical implementation including structured data, and honest reporting about what we can and can't measure yet — rather than chasing speculative "AI SEO" tactics with no evidence behind them. We'd rather tell a client plainly that a metric isn't isolatable yet than hand over a dashboard that implies more precision than actually exists. As the reporting picture around AI Mode matures, we expect the agencies that built on solid content and technical foundations to be the ones best positioned to adapt quickly, rather than needing to start over.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is AI Mode the same as AI Overviews?

No. AI Overviews are automatic AI-generated summaries that can appear above normal results on a standard search page. AI Mode is a separate, dedicated conversational search experience that a user actively opens, built for multi-step, follow-up-question research rather than a single-query summary.

### Is Google AI Mode available in India?

Yes. Google introduced AI Mode in India in Search Labs in June 2025 and opened it to all users shortly after, initially in English. Hindi support followed in September 2025, with further Indian-language support added afterward. Precise details on how deeply it currently covers regional Indian languages are not clearly documented in public sources, so we're not going to state a specific figure.

### Can I track how much traffic comes from AI Mode specifically?

Not cleanly, at least not yet. According to reporting on Google's own Search Console behaviour, AI Mode query data is currently logged together with standard Search data rather than broken out as its own separate channel, so isolating AI Mode-specific performance isn't straightforward with standard tools today.

### Do ads appear inside AI Mode?

Yes, and their presence is growing. Independent research reported by Search Engine Land found ads appearing in close to 30% of commercial queries within AI Mode as of mid-2026, with higher-value keyword categories seeing ads far more often. Google has also introduced new conversational ad formats designed specifically for AI Mode and AI-powered Search.

### Do I need to rewrite all my website content because of AI Mode?

Not necessarily rewrite everything, but a review is worthwhile. Content that already answers a core question clearly, in a well-structured format, with credible authorship and proper schema markup, is generally well-positioned. The bigger wins usually come from filling gaps — pages that only address a narrow query and ignore the natural follow-up questions a real conversation would raise.

### Should a small Pune business worry about AI Mode replacing website traffic entirely?

It's a reasonable long-term consideration rather than an immediate emergency. Some portion of early-stage research can now happen inside an AI Mode conversation without a click-through, but classic organic results, AI Overviews, and paid search all continue to exist alongside AI Mode, and it remains one experience among several rather than a full replacement for Search as it currently stands.

## Where to Start

If you're weighing how much of this actually applies to your business right now, start with three concrete steps: audit your highest-value pages for whether they answer the obvious follow-up questions a reader would ask next, check that your structured data (Organization, LocalBusiness, and FAQ schema where relevant) is implemented correctly, and set a baseline now for impressions, clicks and brand-search volume so you have something to compare against as AI Mode's footprint grows and reporting tools mature. None of this needs to happen overnight, but starting the audit now is better than reacting once the measurement gap closes and everyone else has already adjusted.
